guard_streams.source: One million people have mapped their mobile – have you?
guard_streams.write_limit: Mobile checker usage, predictive mobile coverage and crowdsourced handset experience do not establish fixed-broadband parcel coverage or parcel-measured speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the Map Your Mobile milestone update on 29 May 2026.
Ofcom reported that one million people had used Map Your Mobile.
Map Your Mobile is described as a free mobile coverage checker.
Users enter a postcode to begin comparing mobile networks.
The checker displays a map of networks available in the relevant area.
It includes a score showing which company performs best in the postal district.
The tool is intended to support provider choice before signing up or switching.
The checker uses crowdsourced Opensignal data based on real user experiences.
The checker also uses predictive information from UK mobile networks.
Ofcom states that the checker is regularly updated and allows user feedback.

guard_streams.source: Map Your Mobile – mobile coverage checker update
guard_streams.write_limit: Mobile checker methodology and performance scoring are mobile consumer tools and cannot verify fixed-line service at a selected parcel.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the checker update on 30 June 2025.
The checker update was last revised on 8 August 2025.
The page describes the launch of the new Map Your Mobile coverage checker.
The checker was designed to better reflect likely experience for data-heavy services such as streaming.
The update explains changes made to improve the checker.
The improvements are intended to help consumers choose a provider for locations where they use mobile service.
Ofcom explicitly describes the launch as only a first step.
Ofcom set out further work intended to improve the checker.
The page refers to working with Government and industry on better mobile coverage and performance.
Mobile coverage and performance methodology is not transferred to fixed-broadband parcel accuracy.
